findings.title: Team admin OR owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, so it is only true when the caller is both an admin AND an owner of the team. A team admin who is not the owner (or an owner who is not flagged admin) will be rejected with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests to a team booking, even though the UI offers them the action. This should be `||`.

findings.title: Any existing attendee can add arbitrary guests and trigger organizer-branded emails/calendar updates
findings.body: The authorization check allows any existing attendee of the booking (`isAttendee`) to add new guests. An attendee can therefore add unlimited arbitrary email addresses (the schema has no upper bound on the `guests` array), which causes calendar invitations and 'AttendeeScheduledEmail' emails to be sent from the organizer's identity/calendar to anyone the attendee chooses. Additionally, when an attendee performs the action, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and the `EventManager` are built from the attendee's credentials rather than the organizer's, so `updateCalendarAttendees` either fails or operates on the wrong user's calendar. This should likely be restricted to the organizer/team admins, and credentials should come from the booking organizer.

findings.title: No status check allows adding guests to cancelled/rejected/past bookings
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking without filtering on `status` and never verifies the booking is ACCEPTED/upcoming. Guests can be added to a cancelled or rejected booking, and the emails/ICS sent by `sendAddGuestsEmails` are generated with `status: "CONFIRMED"`, so recipients receive a confirmed calendar invitation for a cancelled event.

findings.title: Duplicate/blacklist checks are case-sensitive and racy, allowing duplicate attendees
findings.body: Existing-attendee dedupe compares `guest === attendee.email` with exact case, while the blacklist is lowercased but the incoming guest is not. 'User@X.com' vs 'user@x.com' bypasses both checks and creates a duplicate Attendee row. There is also no unique constraint enforced transactionally, so two concurrent addGuests calls can both pass the filter and insert duplicate attendees. Normalize emails (lowercase/trim) before comparing and storing.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email opt-out settings
findings.body: Unlike neighboring functions (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, etc.), `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or honor the event type metadata `disableStandardEmails` (host/attendee). Event types configured to suppress standard emails will still send organizer and attendee emails when guests are added.

findings.title: Email failures swallowed with console.log and no error detail
findings.body: The try/catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails` logs only the static string "Error sending AddGuestsEmails" and drops the actual error, and it runs after `updateCalendarAttendees`, which is unguarded. If calendar update throws, the mutation reports failure even though attendees were already committed to the DB, leaving the UI saying the operation failed while guests exist and no emails were sent. At minimum log the error (use the logger with safeStringify like elsewhere) and consider the ordering/partial-failure semantics.

findings.title: No upper bound on guests array enables mass invitation/email abuse
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`, so a single authenticated request can add hundreds of attendees to a booking, each generating calendar invites and emails sent from the organizer's address. Add a reasonable maximum (e.g. `.max(10)`) consistent with the booking flow's guest limits.

findings.title: New addGuests mutation has no tests
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated mutation that mutates booking attendees, updates external calendars, and sends emails, with non-trivial authorization logic (organizer / team admin-owner / attendee), but includes no unit or integration tests. The broken `&&` in the admin/owner check is exactly the kind of defect a permission test would have caught.
